hero.artist: United States Navy, Chief Photographer's Mate Greg McCreash
hero.credit: Navy NewsStand Photo ID: 040213-N-7412M-001Navy NewsStand Home
hero.description: Portsmouth, Va. (Feb. 13, 2004) – The nuclear powered aircraft carrier USS Harry S. Truman (CVN-75) transits the Elizabeth River following completion of a six-month Planned Incremental Availability (PIA) at Norfolk Naval Shipyard. Truman completed her yard period a week ahead of schedule and 4 million dollars under budget.
categories: General views of USS Harry S. Truman (CVN-75)

gallery.title: File:140501-A-ON889-102 (13998056888).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Norfolk District from United States
gallery.description: NORFOLK, Virginia -- Colonel Donald E. Degidio, Jr., deputy commander of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, North Atlantic Division, spends a few hours on the Elizabeth River on the debris removal vessell Harrell with Norfolk District employees. In the background is the Navy's nuclear powered aircraft carrier Harry S. Truman (CVN 75). The North Atlantic Division is one of nine regions providing engineering and construction services to the nation. It is the Corps’ headquarters for the Northeastern United States, Europe, and Africa, with offices in Concord, Mass., New York City, Philadelphia, Baltimore, Norfolk and Wiesbaden, Germany. (U.S. Army photo/Pamela K Spaugy)
